title: Slices of Summer Cake  (Porciones de pastel de verano)

segments.t: En el alegre mostrador del café, Tessa corta porciones doradas, coronadas de rubí, del pastel de verano de bayas y almendras y las sirve en platos de gres, mientras Hannah y Owen regresan a toda prisa con bandejas vacías y los ojos brillantes. Escuchemos primero la escena.
Tell me everything right now — did table one taste the berry almond cake yet?!
He took one small bite, closed both eyes, and tapped his hand over his heart!
Then he nodded twice to Arthur and wrote two words on his napkin: Exact match!
EXACT MATCH! Did you hear that, kitchen ovens?! Honey and orange zest won the day!
Number ten from next door said it tastes like May afternoon sunshine thirty years back.
And every single neighbor clipped their numbered birch clothespin onto their lapel like a badge!
Even that soggy poster accident turned into the hit fashion trend of Linden Street!
Here go six more slices for table three — save two big corners for the musicians!
Listen — Evelyn and Caleb just sat down side by side on the walnut piano bench!
Turn down the tea kettle burner so the whole courtyard hears every single note!
Come stand by the archway with us, Tessa — the ovens earned a five-minute break!
Wiping my hands right now — play us home, Room Nine!
Vamos ahora línea por línea con este triunfo de la cocina.
Tell me everything right now — did table one taste the berry almond cake yet?!

'¡Cuéntenmelo todo ahora mismo! ¿Ya probó la mesa uno el pastel de bayas y almendras?' Tell me everything es la petición impaciente de «cuéntamelo todo», y yet al final de una pregunta significa «ya»:
Tell me everything right now
aplicado aquí al verbo taste, «probar»:
did table one taste the berry almond cake yet
He took one small bite, closed both eyes, and tapped his hand over his heart!
'¡Dio un bocadito, cerró los dos ojos y se dio unos golpecitos con la mano sobre el corazón!' Take a bite es «dar un bocado», y close both eyes, «cerrar los dos ojos»:
He took one small bite, closed both eyes
y tap es «dar golpecitos suaves»:
tapped his hand over his heart
Then he nodded twice to Arthur and wrote two words on his napkin: Exact match!
'Luego asintió dos veces mirando a Arthur y escribió dos palabras en su servilleta: ¡igualito!' Nod es «asentir con la cabeza», y nod to someone es asentir dirigiéndose a esa persona:
he nodded twice to Arthur
y exact match significa «coincidencia exacta, idéntico»:
wrote two words on his napkin: Exact match
EXACT MATCH! Did you hear that, kitchen ovens?! Honey and orange zest won the day!
'¡IGUALITO! ¿¡Lo oyeron, hornos de la cocina!? ¡La miel y la ralladura de naranja se llevaron la victoria!' Tessa habla a sus hornos con un vocativo humorístico, y did you hear that es «¿lo oíste?»:
Did you hear that, kitchen ovens
mientras win the day, con el pasado irregular won, es «llevarse la victoria»:
Honey and orange zest won the day
Number ten from next door said it tastes like May afternoon sunshine thirty years back.
'El del número diez de al lado dijo que sabe a una tarde soleada de mayo de hace treinta años.' Next door significa «de al lado», y taste like es «saber a»:
Number ten from next door
con back como «atrás en el tiempo»:
tastes like May afternoon sunshine thirty years back
And every single neighbor clipped their numbered birch clothespin onto their lapel like a badge!
'¡Y todos los vecinos se prendieron su pinza numerada de abedul en la solapa como una insignia!' Every single refuerza a every: «todos y cada uno»; clip es «sujetar con una pinza»:
every single neighbor clipped their numbered birch clothespin
y lapel es la «solapa» de la chaqueta:
onto their lapel like a badge
Even that soggy poster accident turned into the hit fashion trend of Linden Street!
'¡Hasta aquel accidente del cartel empapado se convirtió en la moda de éxito de la calle Linden!' Soggy significa «empapado, blando de agua», y turn into es «convertirse en»:
that soggy poster accident turned into
con hit como «éxito» y trend como «tendencia»:
the hit fashion trend of Linden Street
Here go six more slices for table three — save two big corners for the musicians!
'Ahí van seis porciones más para la mesa tres: ¡guarden dos esquinas grandes para los músicos!' Here go... es la fórmula para anunciar lo que se envía, y slices son «porciones, rebanadas»:
Here go six more slices for table three
y musician, «músico», termina en -ian como otros oficios:
save two big corners for the musicians
Listen — Evelyn and Caleb just sat down side by side on the walnut piano bench!
'Escuchen: ¡Evelyn y Caleb acaban de sentarse uno al lado del otro en la banqueta del piano de nogal!' Sit down es «sentarse», y sat es su pasado irregular:
Evelyn and Caleb just sat down side by side
sobre la banqueta del piano:
on the walnut piano bench
Turn down the tea kettle burner so the whole courtyard hears every single note!
'¡Bajen el fuego de la tetera para que todo el patio oiga cada una de las notas!' Turn down es lo contrario de turn up: «bajar» el fuego o el volumen:
Turn down the tea kettle burner
y so introduce la finalidad con presente simple:
so the whole courtyard hears every single note
Come stand by the archway with us, Tessa — the ovens earned a five-minute break!
'Ven a quedarte junto al arco con nosotros, Tessa: ¡los hornos se ganaron un descanso de cinco minutos!' Come stand, sin and ni to, es muy coloquial; earn es «ganarse» algo con esfuerzo:
Come stand by the archway with us, Tessa
y el compuesto con guion lleva minute en singular:
the ovens earned a five-minute break
Wiping my hands right now — play us home, Room Nine!
'Me estoy secando las manos ahora mismo: ¡llévanos a casa con tu música, habitación Nueve!' Wipe es «limpiar o secar frotando» con un paño:
Wiping my hands right now
y play us home es una invitación poética a que la música los lleve:
play us home, Room Nine
Escuchemos la escena completa una vez más.
Tell me everything right now — did table one taste the berry almond cake yet?!
He took one small bite, closed both eyes, and tapped his hand over his heart!
Then he nodded twice to Arthur and wrote two words on his napkin: Exact match!
EXACT MATCH! Did you hear that, kitchen ovens?! Honey and orange zest won the day!
Number ten from next door said it tastes like May afternoon sunshine thirty years back.
And every single neighbor clipped their numbered birch clothespin onto their lapel like a badge!
Even that soggy poster accident turned into the hit fashion trend of Linden Street!
Here go six more slices for table three — save two big corners for the musicians!
Listen — Evelyn and Caleb just sat down side by side on the walnut piano bench!
Turn down the tea kettle burner so the whole courtyard hears every single note!
Come stand by the archway with us, Tessa — the ovens earned a five-minute break!
Wiping my hands right now — play us home, Room Nine!

Dos palabras en una servilleta, «idéntico, igualito», coronan el triunfo de la cocina de Tessa justo cuando cuatro manos tocan las teclas del piano de nogal. Nos vemos en la habitación nueve en la próxima escena.
See you next time!
